notes:
The Environment Canada weather mooring at Sentry Shoal in the Northern Strait of Georgia provides a platform of opportunity for collection of high frequency biogeochemical measurements. From spring to fall in 2015, 2016, and 2017, autonomous sensors were
deployed on the mooring to collect surface nitrate, temperature and salinity measurements every 30 minutes. Nitrate concentration was measured using a Satlantic SUNA (Ultraviolet Nitrate Analyzer), temperature and salinity were measured using a SeaBird 37-SMP
MicroCAT. Sensors were deployed each year in the spring and serviced in the field every 2-3 months, following recovery in the fall, sensors were shipped for factory service and calibration.

This project was supported by the Tula Foundation and the Pacific Salmon Foundation, fieldwork was a collaborative effort between the Hakai Institute, and SeaThis Consulting.

notes_translated.en:
The Environment Canada weather mooring at Sentry Shoal in the Northern Strait of Georgia provides a platform of opportunity for collection of high frequency biogeochemical measurements. From spring to fall in 2015, 2016, and 2017, autonomous sensors were
deployed on the mooring to collect surface nitrate, temperature and salinity measurements every 30 minutes. Nitrate concentration was measured using a Satlantic SUNA (Ultraviolet Nitrate Analyzer), temperature and salinity were measured using a SeaBird 37-SMP
MicroCAT. Sensors were deployed each year in the spring and serviced in the field every 2-3 months, following recovery in the fall, sensors were shipped for factory service and calibration.

This project was supported by the Tula Foundation and the Pacific Salmon Foundation, fieldwork was a collaborative effort between the Hakai Institute, and SeaThis Consulting.
notes_translated.fr:
Le poste d'amarrage météorologique d'Environnement Canada à Sentry Shoal, dans le nord du détroit de Géorgie, offre une plate-forme permettant de recueillir des mesures biogéochimiques à haute fréquence. Du printemps à l'automne en 2015, 2016 et 2017, les capteurs autonomes étaient déployés sur le mouillage pour recueillir des mesures de nitrates de surface, de température et de salinité toutes les 30 minutes. La concentration de nitrate a été mesurée à l'aide d'un Satlantic SUNA (analyseur de nitrate ultraviolet), la température et la salinité ont été mesurées à l'aide d'un SeaBird 37-SMP MicroCat. Les capteurs étaient déployés chaque année au printemps et entretenus sur le terrain tous les 2 à 3 mois. Après leur rétablissement à l'automne, les capteurs étaient expédiés pour être entretenus en usine et étalonnés.

Ce projet a été soutenu par la Tula Foundation et la Pacific Salmon Foundation. Le travail de terrain était le fruit d'une collaboration entre l'Institut Hakai et SeaThis Consulting.
